name: Barbell Front Raise
description: The barbell front raise targets the anterior deltoid by raising a barbell from the thighs to shoulder height in front of the body. The bilateral nature and pronated grip load both anterior deltoids simultaneously and provide a simple progressive overload path compared to dumbbell variations. It is a straightforward anterior deltoid isolation exercise suitable for adding volume to shoulder training.

execution.starting_position: Stand upright holding a barbell with a pronated (overhand) grip at approximately shoulder width. The bar hangs at thigh level with arms nearly straight.
execution.setup_instructions: Use a relatively light load. The anterior deltoid is already heavily stressed from pressing — treat this as supplemental volume work.
steps: Step 1: Hold the bar at thigh level with an overhand grip.
Step 2: Keeping the arms nearly straight (slight elbow bend), raise the bar in front of the body.
Step 3: Raise until the bar is at shoulder height or slightly above.
Step 4: Pause at the top briefly.
Step 5: Lower under full control to the thighs.
execution.breathing_instructions: Exhale as you raise, inhale as you lower.
common_mistakes: Using body momentum by leaning back or rocking
Raising too high — above shoulder level recruits the traps excessively
Bending the elbows too much, turning it into a curl-raise hybrid
safety_considerations: Keep the lower back neutral — do not hyperextend as the bar rises
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Thigh level to shoulder height (90 degrees).
coaching_cues: Arms like a robot — controlled arc
